sections.h2: Where is Upper Macungie Township, and how big has it grown?
sections.html:
Upper Macungie is a Lehigh County township about 11.5 miles southwest of Allentown, 60.8 miles northwest of Philadelphia and 99.2 miles west of New York City. It spans 26.3 square miles and was created in 1832 when Macungie Township was divided into Upper and Lower Macungie. Wikipedia lists seven villages: Breinigsville, Fogelsville, Krocksville, Kuhnsville, Newtown, Ruppsville and Trexlertown.

The growth numbers are the story here. The township counted 13,895 people in 2000, 20,063 in 2010 and 26,377 in 2020, a gain of 44.4 percent in the first decade and 31.5 percent in the second. The 2020 census found 9,313 households with an average size of 2.65 people. A township that added so many residents in two decades has plenty of newer housing, so look at what comparable recent homes on your side of the township listed for.

The ZIP codes are 18031, 18051, 18087, 18104 and 18106. Lower Macungie lies to the southeast and South Whitehall to the northeast, while Maxatawny and Longswamp Townships in Berks County border the township on the west and southwest.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and schools in Upper Macungie affect a listing?
sections.html:
Interstate 78 and U.S. 22 cross at exit 49 in Fogelsville, where Pennsylvania Route 100 also meets them. U.S. 222 cuts from southwest to northeast, and PA 100, Interstate 476 and PA 863 carry traffic north and south. Schantz Road links several industrial and commerce parks across the township. As of 2022 the township had 182.81 miles of public roads, with 135.94 miles maintained by the township, 45.97 by PennDOT and 0.90 by the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission. LANta bus routes 213, 218 and 322 serve it.

The Parkland School District covers the township. Grades 9 through 12 attend Parkland High School, and most middle schoolers go to Springhouse Middle School, except those in the far north. Fogelsville, Fred J. Jaindl and Veterans Memorial Elementary Schools are located in the township. Parkland Community Library on Walbert Avenue is free to residents of Upper Macungie, North Whitehall and South Whitehall townships.

  • Spell out the drive to I-78, Route 100 and the industrial parks off Schantz Road.
  • Name the elementary school only after confirming the attendance zone with Parkland.
  • Mention the library, parks and the Lehigh Valley hospital campus if they are close.

sections.h2: Does the weather or land in Upper Macungie matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Freezing Januaries shape the house. Fogelsville averages 28.5 degrees Fahrenheit in January and 73.3 in July, and the township falls in plant hardiness zone 6b. Buyers therefore look hard at the furnace, roof and insulation, and an aging boiler will come up in their inspection.

Water flows to Little Lehigh Creek and Jordan Creek, which both feed the Lehigh River, so walk the lot for low spots and check where downspouts discharge. The township's permit list includes a Low Pressure Sewer System Connection form. A house on that system will draw questions about maintenance, so get the facts from the township before you list.

Farm and forest parcels may be enrolled in Clean and Green, a county program that taxes land on how it is used. Enrolled owners should check the conveyance form the county posts before a sale closes.

sections.h2: What permits and zoning rules affect selling in Upper Macungie?
sections.html:
No resale inspection is listed among the Permit Department's forms. The department works from Suite 311 at 7540 Windsor Drive, keeps weekday hours of 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. and enforces the state's building codes. Its form list covers basements, decks, kitchens, bathrooms, roof re-shingling, water heaters, HVAC replacement, pools, oil tank removal and sheds, and it also lists a Business Use and Occupancy application. Nothing on it covers an ordinary house sale, so call the department and ask what, if anything, your address needs at transfer.

Pennsylvania moved to the 2021 ICC code series for enforcement on January 1, 2026. Work under contracts signed before that date could use the older 2018 code if the permit was filed by June 30, 2026, and anything signed or filed after that must meet the 2021 code. If you have an unfinished project, ask the township which code applies to it.

  • Zoning permits are issued when a use or structure conforms to the zoning ordinance.
  • If the township denies a zoning permit, you can take it to the Zoning Hearing Board, which sits most months on the second and fourth Wednesday evenings.
  • The township wants a hearing application roughly four weeks ahead to meet advertising rules.
  • The township is rewriting its zoning ordinance, and printed copies of the current one cost $35.

sections.h2: What does Lehigh County charge and record when an Upper Macungie house sells?
sections.html:
Your deed gets recorded in the Courthouse in downtown Allentown, in the Recorder of Deeds division on West Hamilton Street, Room 122. Staff are reachable at 610-782-3162 on weekdays. The Commonwealth takes 1 percent of the value at recording, and the county collects a local portion with it. The local portion can be divided between township and school district, so confirm the exact rate for your deed with the Recorder before you run net proceeds.

Lehigh County rules that touch an Upper Macungie sale. Sources: Lehigh County Assessment Office and Recorder of Deeds

Assessment base year2013, set at full market value

Conveyances among spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings are generally exempt. A statement of value form goes with any deed that claims another exemption or leaves out the full price. Deeds are public record, so the county cannot keep a sale price out of print.

sections.h2: How does the Lehigh County assessment and appeal work for Upper Macungie owners?
sections.html:
Values at the Lehigh County Assessment Office trace back to the 2013 countywide reassessment, which set assessments at the full fair market value of that year. An owner who disagrees files with the county Board of Assessment Appeals. The yearly cutoff is August 1, and the Board wants the original signed form and fee in hand by then. A mailed postmark or a fax does not prove a timely filing, so deliver the paper yourself or mail it well ahead.

A newer state law, Act 29 of 2026, signed July 20, 2026, adds a duty for buyers who will not live in the home: they must send the county a contact record within a month of purchase. An investor who buys your house will handle that after closing. County assessment staff can be reached at 610-782-3038.

Township and school tax rates come from the township office and the Parkland School District tax office, so pull your latest bill before you price the house.

sections.h2: How can I sell an Upper Macungie house quickly?
sections.html:
Most owners weigh a traditional listing against a direct sale to a buyer who pays cash and takes the house in its current state. With so much newer housing around you, buyers compare condition closely, and a dated or worn property may fit a cash buyer better.

  • A listing suits a recently updated house and an owner who is fine with weeks of showings and lender timelines.
  • A direct sale suits an inherited house, a tenant-occupied one, or a seller with a fixed moving date.
  • Collect permit records for any finished basement, deck or kitchen project, because buyers and title agents ask for them.

Get each offer in writing and compare what you would actually net after transfer tax, fees and repairs.

faqs.q: Is a resale inspection part of closing on an Upper Macungie house?
faqs.a: The Permit Department's forms list shows no residential resale inspection. Call the department to learn whether your address needs anything, and close out any open permits before listing.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Upper Macungie Township?
faqs.a: Parkland School District. Students in grades 9 through 12 attend Parkland High School, and most middle schoolers attend Springhouse Middle School. Confirm your attendance zone with the district.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for contesting an Upper Macungie assessment?
faqs.a: August 1 each year for annual appeals. The Board needs the original signed form and fee in its hands by then, and it gives no credit for a fax or a postmark.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies when an Upper Macungie house sells?
faqs.a: The state takes 1 percent, and the county adds a local portion when the deed is recorded. Call the Recorder of Deeds at 610-782-3162 to confirm the local figure for your property.

faqs.q: What if my Upper Macungie land is enrolled in Clean and Green?
faqs.a: Talk to the county Assessment Office before signing a contract. The program taxes qualifying land on its use value and generally starts at ten acres, and the county posts a conveyance form for land that changes hands.
